'''Luis Suárez Miramontes''' ({{IPA|es|ˈlwis ˈswaɾeθ miɾaˈmontes}}; 2 May 1935 – 9 July 2023<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |last=Iglesias |first=Denís |date=9 July 2023 |title=Muere Luis Suárez, el 'Arquitecto' que dio un Balón de Oro a España |url=https://www.diariocordoba.com/deportes/2023/07/09/muere-luis-suarez-unico-espanol-89659727.html |access-date=10 July 2023 |website=Diario Córdoba |language=es}}</ref>) was a Spanish professional [[association football|footballer]] and manager. He played as a [[midfielder]] for [[Deportivo de La Coruña]], [[CD Condal|España Industrial]], [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]], [[Inter Milan]], [[UC Sampdoria|Sampdoria]]; he also represented the [[Spain national football team|Spain national team]] between 1957 and 1972. Widely regarded as one of the greatest Spanish football players of all time,<ref name="profile" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=9 July 2023 |title=Muere Luis Suárez, el primer Balón de Oro español |url=https://as.com/futbol/primera/muere-luis-suarez-el-primer-balon-de-oro-espanol-n/ |access-date=9 July 2023 |website=[[Diario AS]] |language=es-ES}}</ref> Suárez was noted for his elegant and fluid style of play and also regarded to be one of the greatest midfielders in the history of the sport.<ref name="profile">{{Cite web |title=Luis Suárez |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/club/historia/jugadors_de_llegenda/suarez.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20100202005716/http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/club/historia/jugadors_de_llegenda/suarez.html |archive-date=2 February 2010 |access-date=21 December 2015 |website=FCBarcelona.cat}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.sportskeeda.com/football/10-greatest-midfielders-in-football-history/10 |title=10 greatest midfielders in football history: #1 Lothar Matthaus |website=sportskeeda.com |publisher=[[Sportskeeda]] |first=Ashwin |last=Hanagudu |date=17 September 2016 |access-date=6 November 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Cormack |first=James |date=8 July 2024 |title=The best midfielders of all time |url=https://www.90min.com/best-midfielders-of-all-time |access-date=30 November 2024 |website=90min.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |author1=Mark White |date=5 February 2025 |title=Ranked! The 100 best football players of all time |url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/features/ranked-the-100-best-football-players-of-all-time/7 |access-date=5 February 2025 |website=fourfourtwo.com |language=en}}</ref>

Nicknamed {{lang|es|El Arquitecto}}<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":9">{{Cite web |last=Relaño |first=Alfredo |date=9 July 2023 |title=Adiós, arquitecto |url=https://as.com/futbol/2023/07/09/reportajes/1688891065_616586.html |access-date=10 July 2023 |website=Diario AS |language=es-ES}}</ref> – The Architect –  or {{lang|es|Luisito}},<ref name=":6">{{cite web |date=4 December 2010 |title=Luis Suárez descubre una placa más "tocante" que el Balón de Oro |url=http://www.marca.com/2010/12/04/futbol/mas_futbol/1291480722.html |access-date=10 July 2023 |website=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]] |language=es-ES}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Cecere |first=Nicola |date=9 July 2023 |title=Ciao Luisito. Si è spento a 88 anni Suarez, il regista della Grande Inter |url=https://www.gazzetta.it/Calcio/09-07-2023/morto-luis-suarez-l-inter-piange-il-suo-grande-regista.shtml |access-date=9 July 2023 |website=[[La Gazzetta dello Sport]] |language=it-IT}}</ref> in 1960 Suárez became the first Spanish-born player to win the [[1960 Ballon d'Or|Ballon d'Or]].<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":14">{{Cite web |last=Cáceres |first=Javier |date=9 July 2023 |title=Nachruf zum Tod von Luis Suárez: "Halb Tänzer, halb Torero" |url=https://www.sueddeutsche.de/sport/luis-suarez-inter-legende-gestorben-nachruf-1.6012672 |access-date=10 July 2023 |website=[[Süddeutsche Zeitung]] |language=de}}</ref>{{refn|group=nb|name=bdo|[[Alfredo Di Stéfano]], who won the [[Ballon d'Or]] twice after taking [[Spanish nationality law|Spanish nationality]] in 1956, was born in [[Argentina]].}} In 1964, he helped [[Spain national football team|Spain]] win their first [[1964 European Nations' Cup|European Championship]] title.<ref name=":8">{{Cite news |date=9 July 2023 |title=Luis Suárez, former Barcelona and Internazionale midfielder, dies aged 88 |language=en-GB |work=[[The Guardian]] |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2023/jul/09/luis-suarez-former-barcelona-and-internazionale-midfielder-dies-aged-88 |access-date=9 July 2023 |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> Suárez originally achieved prominence as a creative [[inside forward]], or [[attacking midfielder]] in modern terms, during his spell at Barcelona in the 1950s,<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":20" /> before reaching his prime as a [[deep-lying playmaker]] at Inter Milan, where he played a pivotal role in the success of [[Helenio Herrera]]'s side, and was one of the primary creative forces in the squad, thanks to his skill on the ball, vision, and passing range.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":20">{{cite web |last=Tighe |first=Sam |date=16 April 2013 |title=Great Team Tactics: Breaking Down Helenio Herrera's 'La Grande Inter' |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1606149-great-team-tactics-breaking-down-helenio-herreras-la-grande-inter |access-date=15 September 2014 |website=[[Bleacher Report]]}}</ref> He retired as a player in 1973, after three seasons at Sampdoria.<ref name=":8" />

Suárez subsequently began a career as a coach and managed Inter Milan on three occasions, the latter two of which on a [[Caretaker manager|caretaker]] basis.<ref name=":0" /> He was also at the helm of both the [[Spain national under-21 football team|Spain under-21 national team]], which he led to a [[UEFA European Under-21 Championship|European Under-21 Championship]] title in 1986,<ref name=":14" /><ref name=":10">{{Cite web |last=Besa |first=Ramon |date=9 July 2023 |title=Muere Luis Suárez, leyenda del fútbol español y Balón de Oro |url=https://elpais.com/deportes/2023-07-09/muere-luis-suarez-leyenda-del-futbol-y-balon-de-oro.html |access-date=10 July 2023 |website=[[El País]] |language=es-ES}}</ref> and the [[Spain national football team|Spanish senior national team]], which he led to the round of 16 of the [[1990 FIFA World Cup|1990 World Cup]].<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":0" /> He died in [[Milan]] on 9 July 2023, aged 88.<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":0" />

==Club career==

=== Early life and Deportivo La Coruña ===

Luis Suárez Miramontes was born on 2 May 1935, in [[A Coruña]], [[Galicia (Spain)|Galicia]];<ref name=":9" /><ref name=":6" /> the last of three brothers,<ref name=":9" /> he was raised in the {{lang|es|[[barrio]]}} of Monte Alto, where his family owned a [[Butcher|butcher shop]].<ref name=":15">{{Cite web |last=Balado |first=Lois |date=2 May 2020 |title=De la carnicería a arquitecto mundial del fútbol; Luis Suárez cumple 85 años |url=https://www.lavozdegalicia.es/noticia/torremarathon/2020/05/02/carniceria-arquitecto-mundial-futbol-luis-suarez-cumple-85-anos/00031588433238354574222.htm |access-date=10 July 2023 |website=[[La Voz de Galicia]] |language=es-ES}}</ref><ref name=":16">{{Cite web |last=Ruiz |first=Marco |date=18 December 2016 |title="Di Stéfano, Charlton, Kopa..., era duro ser Balón de Oro" |url=https://as.com/futbol/2016/12/18/internacional/1482035019_630849.html |access-date=10 July 2023 |website=Diario AS |language=es-ES}}</ref>

He started playing football at Perseverancia, a local team administered by the Santo Tomás [[parish]];<ref name=":16" /><ref name=":12">{{Cite web |last=Canibe |first=Álvaro |date=6 December 2019 |title=Así fue la carrera de Luis Suárez, único Balón de Oro español |url=https://as.com/futbol/2019/11/29/fotorrelato/1575056451_841148.html |access-date=10 July 2023 |website=Diario AS |language=es-ES}}</ref> in 1949, aged 14, he joined [[Deportivo de La Coruña|Deportivo La Coruña]],<ref name=":9" /><ref name=":17">{{Cite web |date=9 July 2023 |title=Luis Suárez, exjugador y exentrenador del Deportivo y mito del fútbol mundial, fallece a los 88 anos |url=https://www.rcdeportivo.es/noticias/luis-suarez-exjugador-y-exentrenador-del-deportivo-y-mito-del-futbol-mundial-fallece-a-los-88-anos |access-date=10 July 2023 |website=[[Deportivo La Coruña|RC Deportivo]] |language=es-ES}}</ref> following a successful trial he had attended after reading an advertisement left on {{lang|es|[[La Voz de Galicia]]}} by manager [[Alejandro Scopelli]], who was helping the club establish a youth academy.<ref name=":16" /><ref name=":49">{{Cite web |last=Fernández |first=Xurxo |date=9 July 2023 |title=Luisito Suárez Miramontes, la estrella del Campo de la Luna |url=https://www.lavozdegalicia.es/noticia/deportes/2023/07/09/luisito-suarez-miramontes-estrella-campo-luna/00031688906536381210633.htm |access-date=23 August 2023 |website=La Voz de Galicia |language=es-ES}}</ref>

After coming through the club's youth ranks and playing for their reserve team, [[Deportivo Fabril]],<ref name=":17" /> Suárez was promoted to the first team during the [[1953–54 La Liga|1953–54 season]],<ref name=":9" /><ref name=":17" /> as part of a squad that was managed by [[Carlos Iturraspe]],<ref name=":9" /><ref name=":18">{{Cite web |date=21 March 2018 |title="Luis, ¿firmaste por el Barcelona?" |url=https://www.lavozdegalicia.es/noticia/torremarathon/2018/03/21/luis-suarez/00031521658018423617274.htm |access-date=10 July 2023 |website=La Voz de Galicia |language=es-ES}}</ref> and included players such as [[Pahiño]] and [[Arsenio Iglesias]].<ref name=":16" /><ref name=":18" /> On 6 December 1953, he made his senior debut for Deportivo, starting in a 6–1 league defeat to [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] at the [[Camp de Les Corts]].<ref name=":15" /><ref name=":17" /> Throughout the rest of the campaign, he established himself as a regular starter for the Galician club,<ref name=":9" /> attracting interest by both [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] and [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]].<ref name=":16" /> He played 17 games and scored three goals for Deportivo.<ref name=":15" /><ref name=":17" />

=== Barcelona ===
In March 1954, Suárez joined fellow [[La Liga]] side [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]], together with team-mate [[Dagoberto Moll]],<ref name=":17" /><ref name=":18" /> for a reported total fee of 600,000 [[Spanish peseta|pesetas]].<ref name=":49" /> The two players were officially registered by the Catalan club at the end of [[1953–54 La Liga|1953–54 league season]], and as such deemed eligible to play in the [[1954 Copa del Generalísimo|Copa del Generalísimo]] of the same year.<ref name=":9" /><ref name=":17" />{{refn|group=nb|name=sc|At the time, the [[Spanish Cup]] took place right after the end of the [[La Liga|league season]].}} He made his debut for Barça on 2 May 1954, the day of his 19th birthday,<ref name=":3" /> in a 4–0 victory over his former team Deportivo in the cup's first round;<ref name=":9" /> he then served as a regular starter for [[Ferdinand Daučík]]'s side throughout the rest of the competition,<ref name=":9" /> as they eventually lost to [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] in the [[1954 Copa del Generalísimo final|final]].<ref name=":9" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Velasco |first=Santiago |title=Copa del Rey / Spanish Cup 1954 |url=http://www.linguasport.com/futbol/nacional/copa/copa54.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20030916224716/http://www.linguasport.com/futbol/nacional/copa/Copa54.htm |url-status=usurped |archive-date=16 September 2003 |access-date=10 July 2023 |website=LinguaSport |language=es-ES}}</ref>
[[File:LuisSuarezMiramontes1960.webp|alt=Suárez with Barcelona in 1960.|thumb|Suárez with [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] in 1960]]
During the [[1954–55 La Liga|1954–55 season]], the midfielder gained limited playing time with the first team,<ref name=":16" /> under manager [[Sandro Puppo]],<ref name=":9" /><ref name=":19">{{Cite web |last=Giménez |first=Santi |date=9 July 2023 |title=El peor error de la historia del Barça |url=https://as.com/futbol/primera/el-peor-error-de-la-historia-del-barca-n/ |access-date=10 July 2023 |website=Diario AS |language=es-ES}}</ref> while also featuring for Barcelona's reserve side, [[CD Condal|España Industrial]], in the [[Segunda División|second division]].<ref name=":9" /> Throughout the following campaigns, he steadily established himself as a regular starter,<ref name=":9" /> although some of his coaches considered him "too frail" physically,<ref name=":19" /> with manager [[Ferenc Plattkó]] notably forcing him to do extra work-out on a [[punching bag]] in order to raise his [[muscle mass]].<ref name=":9" /><ref name=":21">{{Cite web |last=Suárez Miramontes |first=Luis |date=30 September 2019 |title=EN PRIMERA PERSONA: Luis Suárez Miramontes |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.es/es/noticias/1358023/en-primera-persona-luis-suarez-miramontes |access-date=11 July 2023 |website=FC Barcelona |language=es-ES}}</ref> At the end of the 1956–57 season, he won his first [[1957 Copa del Generalísimo|Spanish Cup]] with the club.<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":31">{{Cite news |last=Glanville |first=Brian |date=10 July 2023 |title=Luis Suárez obituary |language=en-GB |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2023/jul/10/luis-suarez-obituary |access-date=13 July 2023 |issn=0261-3077}}</ref>

Following the appointment of [[Helenio Herrera]] as Barça's manager at the start of the 1958–59 season,<ref name=":9" /> Suárez started performing at a consistently high level in the [[inside forward|left inside forward]] position,<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":16" /><ref name=":22">{{Cite web |date=9 July 2023 |title=Luis Suárez: estrella de España en la primera EURO |url=https://es.uefa.com/euro2024/news/0253-0d8014195f1a-06ef86012a6d-1000--luis-suarez-estrella-de-espana-en-la-primera-euro/ |access-date=11 July 2023 |website=[[UEFA]] |language=es}}</ref> becoming one of the most important players in a team that also included [[Ladislao Kubala]], [[Zoltán Czibor]], [[Sándor Kocsis]], [[Ramón Alberto Villaverde|Ramón Villaverde]], [[Justo Tejada]], [[Evaristo (footballer)|Evaristo]] and [[Eulogio Martínez]], among others.<ref name=":9" /><ref name=":22" /> With Herrera as coach, the club and Suárez won a domestic [[1958–59 La Liga|league]]–[[1958–59 Copa del Generalísimo|cup]] double in the 1958–59 season,<ref name=":9" /><ref name=":22" /> and then a [[1959–60 La Liga|league]]–[[1958–60 Inter-Cities Fairs Cup|Fairs Cup]] double in the following campaign,<ref name=":7" /><ref name=":23">{{Cite web |last=Relaño |first=Alfredo |date=25 May 2016 |title=Luis Suárez ficha por el Inter (1961) |url=https://as.com/futbol/2016/05/25/mas_futbol/1464162528_251171.html |access-date=11 July 2023 |website=Diario AS |language=es-ES}}</ref> when they also reached the [[1959–60 European Cup|European Cup]] semi-finals.<ref name=":9" /><ref name=":23" />

However, during his stint under the French manager, Suárez's relationship with Barcelona fans progressively deteriorated, due to a perceived rivalry between him and Kubala;<ref name=":16" /><ref name=":19" /> as a result, the midfielder started getting booed by his own supporters in every game he played.<ref name=":21" /><ref name=":24">{{Cite news |last=Verdú |first=Daniel |date=6 November 2018 |title=Luis Suárez: "En el fútbol de hoy se pierden las raíces" |language=es-ES |work=El País |url=https://elpais.com/deportes/2018/11/04/actualidad/1541318560_969602.html |access-date=11 July 2023 |issn=1134-6582}}</ref>

On 19 October 1960, Suárez scored a goal after a solo action from over the middle of the pitch in a 4–3 [[1960–61 Inter-Cities Fairs Cup|Fairs Cup]] win over [[GNK Dinamo Zagreb|Zagreb XI]].<ref name=":14" /> On 9 November 1960, he scored 1000th [[UEFA Champions League|European Cup]] goal in history in a First round 2–2 [[El Clásico]] draw. In December of the same year, Suárez received the [[1960 Ballon d'Or|Ballon d'Or]] by French magazine {{lang|fr|[[France Football]]}},<ref name=":25">{{Cite web |date=9 July 2023 |title=Pionero Luis Suárez: 60 años del primer Balón de Oro del Barça |url=https://www.sport.es/es/noticias/barca/pionero-luis-suarez-anos-del-primer-balon-oro-del-barca-8236338 |access-date=11 July 2023 |website=sport.es |language=es-ES}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=9 July 2023 |title=Luis Suarez, Ballon d'Or 1960, est mort |url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Luis-suarez-ballon-d-or-1960-est-mort/1407432 |access-date=11 July 2023 |website=[[L'Équipe]] |language=fr-FR}}</ref> with a total of 54 votes.<ref name=":9" /><ref name=":2" /> In the process, he became the first Spanish-born footballer to ever win the prize;<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":7">{{Cite news |date=9 July 2023 |title=Er war einst der beste Fußballer Europas – Luis Suárez Miramontes ist gestorben |language=de |work=[[Der Spiegel]] |url=https://www.spiegel.de/sport/fussball/fussball-luis-suarez-miramontes-ist-mit-88-jahren-gestorben-ikone-beim-fc-barcelona-und-inter-mailand-a-b49f17de-ef56-4513-a48c-2362cf8b4718 |access-date=10 July 2023 |issn=2195-1349}}</ref>{{refn|group=nb|name=bdo}} after [[Alexia Putellas]]'s back-to-back victories in [[2021 Ballon d'Or|2021]] and [[2022 Ballon d'Or|2022]], he retained the title as the only Spanish-born men's footballer to ever receive the award.<ref name=":10" /><ref name=":44">{{Cite web |last=Mata |first=Jesús |date=9 July 2023 |title=Adiós a Luis Suárez, el 'Arquitecto' y primer Balón de Oro nacido en España |url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/liga-italiana/2023/07/09/64aa6beb22601d035b8b45cc.html |access-date=11 July 2023 |website=Marca |language=es-ES}}</ref> Suárez received the Ballon d'Or on 9 March 1961,<ref name=":10" /> just a few minutes before the start of a [[1960–61 European Cup|European Cup]] match against [[Spartak Hradec Králové]].<ref name=":25" />

During his last season at Barcelona, which saw [[Enric Rabassa]], [[Ljubiša Broćić|Ljubisa Brocic]] and [[Enrique Orizaola]] take turns to sit in the dug-out, after Herrera had left for [[Inter Milan]], Suárez did not win any trophy.<ref name=":19" /> Nevertheless, the team reached the [[1961 European Cup Final|final]] of the [[1960–61 European Cup|European Cup]],<ref name=":9" /> where they eventually suffered a 3–2 loss to [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]]:<ref name=":26">{{Cite news |last=Relaño |first=Alfredo |date=8 June 2015 |title=Aquella final de los postes cuadrados |language=es |work=El País |url=https://elpais.com/deportes/2015/06/07/actualidad/1433693500_198936.html |access-date=11 July 2023 |issn=1134-6582}}</ref> it was the midfielder's last game for the Catalan club.<ref name=":23" /><ref name=":24" />

Throughout seven seasons, Suárez played a total number of 253 matches for Barcelona, scoring 141 goals.<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":7" />

=== Inter Milan ===

[[File:1960s Inter Milan - Luis Suárez Miramontes.jpg|thumb|Suárez with [[Inter Milan]] at [[San Siro]] in the mid-1960s]]

On 26 May 1961, five days before the [[1961 European Cup Final|final]] of the [[1960–61 European Cup|European Cup]],<ref name=":26" /> Barcelona and Italian club [[Inter Milan]] reached an agreement for the transfer of Suárez for 25 million Spanish pesetas<ref name=":19" /><ref name=":23" /> ([[Pound sterling|£]]152,000).<ref name=":31" /><ref name=":29">{{Cite news |date=1 September 2013 |title=History of the world transfer record |language=en-GB |work=[[BBC Sport]] |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/23903470 |access-date=10 July 2023}}</ref> He subsequently became the [[World football transfer record|world's most expensive footballer]],<ref name=":7" /><ref name=":29" /> having overtaken the previous record set by [[Omar Sívori]] in 1957.<ref name=":29" /> He also became the first Spanish footballer to play in [[Serie A]],<ref name=":30">{{cite book |last1=Galasso |first1=Vito |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=eB65DwAAQBAJ&pg=PA157 |title=La storia della grande Inter in 501 domande e risposte |date=2019 |publisher=Newton Compton Editori |isbn=978-88-227-3910-0 |page=157 |language=it}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=9 July 2023 |title=Inter's memory for Luis Suarez |url=https://www.inter.it/en/news/inter-memory-luis-suarez |access-date=28 July 2023 |website=[[Inter Milan]] |language=en}}</ref> along with [[Juan Santisteban]].<ref name=":30" /> The transfer, which saw Suárez re-unite with manager Herrera,<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":7" /> has been considered one of the most controversial decisions in Barcelona's history,<ref name=":14" /><ref name=":19" /> as the Catalan club's board reportedly aimed to maximize the revenue in order to repay part of their financial debts,<ref name=":19" /><ref name=":23" /> as well as complete the construction of the [[Camp Nou]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":19" />

On 27 August 1961, he made his debut and scored his first goal for Inter Milan in a 6–0 [[1961–62 Serie A|league]] win over [[Atalanta BC|Atalanta]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Cattini |first=Leo |date=28 August 1961 |title=Brillante esordio dell'Inter che travolge l'Atalanta: 6-0 |language=it-IT |pages=5 |work=[[La Stampa]] |url=http://www.archiviolastampa.it/component/option,com_lastampa/task,search/mod,libera/action,viewer/Itemid,3/page,5/articleid,0081_02_1961_0203A_0005_24673293/ |access-date=28 July 2023}}</ref> In October of the same year, he suffered a knee injury in a [[1961–62 Inter-Cities Fairs Cup|Fairs Cup]] match against [[1. FC Köln|Köln]], which limited his impact on the pitch during the rest of his first season in Italy.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Cattini |first=Leo |date=26 October 1961 |title=L'Inter, malgrado un infortunio a Suarez elimina il Colonia dalla Coppa delle Fiere |language=it-IT |pages=8 |work=[[La Stampa]] |url=http://www.archiviolastampa.it/component/option,com_lastampa/task,search/mod,libera/action,viewer/Itemid,3/page,8/articleid,0082_01_1961_0254_0008_17188136/}}</ref> He finished second in the final ranking for the [[1961 Ballon d'Or]], behind only winner Omar Sívori.<ref name=":32" /><ref name=":50">{{Cite web |last=Andrade |first=Alfonso |date=15 July 2023 |title=Luis Suárez, ¿y ese quién es? |url=https://www.lavozdegalicia.es/noticia/coruna/2023/07/15/luis-suarez-/0003_202307H15C4995.htm |access-date=23 August 2023 |website=La Voz de Galicia |language=es-ES}}</ref>

At the start of [[1962–63 Serie A|the following campaign]],<ref name=":0" /> manager Herrera moved Suárez to the [[deep-lying playmaker]] role,<ref name=":9" /><ref name=":0" /> where he became one of the key players of the {{lang|it|[[Grande Inter]]}} side that famously adopted a counter-attacking style of play.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":20" /><ref name=":16" /> On 10 March 1963, he scored three goals in a 6–0 league win over [[Genoa C.F.C.|Genoa]]: in the process, he became the first Spanish player to ever score a hat-trick in Serie A, and remained the only one to have ever done so until [[Suso (footballer)|Suso]] hit the same achievement in 2016.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Cerezo |first1=Hugo |last2=Prada |first2=Jon |date=4 April 2016 |title=Luis Suárez: "Enhorabuena Suso, ahora estamos dos en el club" |language=es |trans-title=Luis Suárez: "Congratulations Suso, now we are in a two-person club" |publisher=Marca |url=http://www.marca.com/futbol/espanoles-mundo/2016/04/04/5702543f46163fd9178b45a0.html |access-date=4 April 2016}}</ref> At the end of the 1962–63 season, the midfielder won his first national title with Inter.<ref name=":31" /><ref name=":33" />

In the 1963–64 season, although Inter Milan lost the [[1963–64 Serie A|league]] title to [[Bologna FC 1909|Bologna]] in the final tie-breaker,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brera |first=Gianni |date=13 February 2009 |title=Lo spareggio scudetto raccontato da Gianni Brera |url=https://www.repubblica.it/2009/02/sport/calcio/gianni-brera/gianni-brera/gianni-brera.html |access-date=28 July 2023 |website=[[la Repubblica]] |language=it-IT}}</ref> Suárez helped the {{lang|it|Nerazzurri}} win the [[1963–64 European Cup|European Cup]].<ref name=":9" /><ref name=":4" /> In the second leg of the cup's [[1963–64 European Cup#Semi-finals|semi-finals]] against [[Borussia Dortmund]], the midfielder caused controversy after violently kicking the opposing right-half and injuring him, with referee [[Branko Tesanić]] eventually opting against sending the Spanish player off.<ref name=":31" /> He then went on to feature in the [[1964 European Cup final|final]] in [[Vienna]],<ref name=":31" /> where Inter gained a 3–1 win over Real Madrid to win the European title.<ref name=":22" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Ortego |first=Enrique |date=23 November 2020 |title=Cuando el Inter jubiló a Di Stéfano |url=https://elpais.com/deportes/2020-11-23/cuando-el-inter-jubilo-a-di-stefano.html |url-access=registration |access-date=28 July 2023 |website=El País |language=es-ES}}</ref>

On 26 September 1964, Suárez was a part of the Inter side that won the [[1964 Intercontinental Cup]], having gained a 1–0 victory [[Overtime (sports)#Association football|after extra time]] over [[Club Atlético Independiente|Independiente]] in the tie-breaking match.<ref name=":34" /><ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=27 September 1964 |title=El Inter de Milán se adjudicó la Copa Intercontinental de clubs |url=http://biblioteca.galiciana.gal/es/catalogo_imagenes/grupo.do?path=1281655&posicion=6&presentacion=pagina |access-date=28 July 2023 |website=Galiciana |publisher=El Progreso |page=6 |language=es-ES}}</ref> In December of the same year, he finished second in the final standings for the [[1964 Ballon d'Or]], behind winner [[Denis Law]],<ref name=":10" /><ref name=":35" /> with the Spanish player publicly expressing his disappointment over this outcome on multiple occasions during his lifetime.<ref name=":14" /><ref name=":10" /><ref name=":16" /> After winning his second [[1964–65 Serie A|league title]] with Inter<ref name=":31" /><ref name=":36" /> – and being voted as the best player of the season by the Italian sporting press – ,<ref>{{Cite web |date=8 July 1965 |title=El mejor de Italia |url=http://biblioteca.galiciana.gal/es/catalogo_imagenes/grupo.do?path=1116269&posicion=12&presentacion=pagina |access-date=28 July 2023 |website=Galiciana |publisher=El Pueblo Gallego |page=12 |language=es-ES}}</ref> Suárez also helped the Italian club claim their second consecutive [[1964–65 European Cup|European Cup]],<ref name=":4" /> thanks to a 1–0 over [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] in the [[1965 European Cup final|final]].<ref name=":31" /><ref name=":37" />

On 25 August 1965, Suárez took part in a [[Friendly match|friendly]] match against his former club Barcelona at the Camp Nou:<ref name=":10" /> at the 38th minute of the match,<ref name=":9" /> he abruptly left the pitch after being on the receiving end of boos from {{lang|ca|blaugrana}} supporters since the start of the game, and made a ''[[bras d'honneur]]'' towards them before reaching the exit,<ref name=":10" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Pereda |first=Chus |date=6 February 2009 |title=Un episodio más de la pelea entre kubalistas y suaristas |url=https://as.com/opinion/2009/02/06/portada/1233950165_850215.html |access-date=23 August 2023 |website=Diario AS |language=es-ES}}</ref> a gesture he eventually came to regret throughout the years.<ref name=":21" /> On 8 September of the same year, he once again helped Inter Milan beat Independiente to lift their second [[1965 Intercontinental Cup|Intercontinental Cup]] in a row.<ref name=":38" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=9 July 2023 |title=FC Barcelona and Inter Milan legend Luis Suárez's trophy haul |url=https://www.sport.es/en/news/barca/fc-barcelona-and-inter-milan-legend-luis-suarezs-trophy-haul-89661984 |access-date=11 July 2023 |website=sport.es |language=en}}</ref> In December of the same year, he was the third most-voted player in the final ranking of the [[1965 Ballon d'Or]], behind team-mate [[Giacinto Facchetti]] and winner [[Eusébio]].<ref name=":50" /><ref name=":39" /> Throughout the [[1965–66 Serie A|1965–66 league campaign]], Suárez scored five goals,<ref name=":40" /> helping Inter lift their second consecutive national title;<ref name=":31" /><ref name=":40" /> his team also reached the semi-finals of the [[1965–66 European Cup|European Cup]], before losing to eventual champions Real Madrid.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ross |first=James M. |date=18 July 2023 |title=European Competitions 1965-66 |url=https://www.rsssf.org/ec/ec196566.html |access-date=23 August 2023 |website=RSSSF}}</ref>

In May 1967, Suárez was forced to miss the [[1967 European Cup final|European Cup final]] against [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] due to an injury, being subsequently replaced by [[Mauro Bicicli]]:<ref>{{cite news |date=4 June 2017 |title=The Scotsman's match preview of Celtic's 1967 European Cup victory |work=[[The Scotsman]] |url=https://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/teams/celtic/the-scotsman-s-match-preview-of-celtic-s-1967-european-cup-victory-1-4454536/ |access-date=23 August 2023}}</ref> Inter eventually suffered a 2–1 defeat.<ref>{{cite news |last=Barham |first=Albert |date=25 May 1967 |title=Relentless attack captures European Cup |work=The Guardian |location=London |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/1967/may/25/championsleague.sport |access-date=23 August 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Spencer |first=Stuart |date=25 May 2017 |title=The Day Lisbon Belonged to Celtic |url=https://scottishfootballmuseum.org.uk/the-day-lisbon-belonged-to-celtic/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210118203119/https://scottishfootballmuseum.org.uk/the-day-lisbon-belonged-to-celtic/ |archive-date=18 January 2021 |access-date=23 August 2023 |publisher=[[Scottish Football Museum]]}}</ref> In the following weeks, the Italian club also missed out on their third [[1966–67 Serie A|national title]] in a row on the last day (in favor of [[Juventus FC|Juventus]]),<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bagnati |first=Giuseppe |date=5 May 2008 |title=Cadè, lo scippa-scudetti: "Oggi è tutto diverso" |url=https://www.gazzetta.it/Calcio/SerieA/Primo_Piano/2008/05_Maggio/15/cade.shtml |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081105134030/https://www.gazzetta.it/Calcio/SerieA/Primo_Piano/2008/05_Maggio/15/cade.shtml |archive-date=5 November 2008 |access-date=23 August 2023 |publisher=[[Gazzetta dello Sport]] |language=it-IT}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Accatino |first=Giulio |date=2 June 1967 |title=Il dramma dell'Inter battuta a Mantova |url=http://www.archiviolastampa.it/component/option,com_lastampa/task,search/mod,libera/action,viewer/Itemid,3/page,9/articleid,0019_01_1967_0129_0009_6584769/ |access-date=23 August 2023 |publisher=La Stampa |page=9 |language=it-IT}}</ref> and got eliminated by [[Calcio Padova|Padova]] in the [[1966–67 Coppa Italia|Coppa Italia]] semi-finals: as a result, they finished the campaign without winning a single trophy.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Accatino |first=Giulio |date=8 June 1967 |title=Crollo degli interisti su un campo di Serie B |url=http://www.archiviolastampa.it/component/option,com_lastampa/task,search/mod,libera/action,viewer/Itemid,3/page,11/articleid,0019_01_1967_0134_0011_9345036/ |access-date=23 August 2023 |publisher=La Stampa |page=11 |language=it-IT}}</ref>

During the [[1969–70 Serie A|1969–70 campaign]], his last season at Inter Milan, Suárez's performances declined due to his deployment as a [[Sweeper (association football)|sweeper]]:<ref name=":31" /> he scored just one goal in the league, as his side finished runners-up behind [[Cagliari Calcio|Cagliari]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mariani |first=Maurizio |date=26 October 2000 |title=Italy 1969/70 |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesi/ital70.html |access-date=23 August 2023 |website=RSSSF}}</ref>

Between 1961 and 1970, Suárez made a total amount 333 appearances for Inter, scoring 55 goals.<ref name=":0" />[[File:Luis Suárez Miramontes - UC Sampdoria.jpg|thumb|Suárez with [[UC Sampdoria|Sampdoria]] in the early 1970s]]

=== Sampdoria and retirement ===
In July 1970, Suárez was signed by fellow Serie A club [[UC Sampdoria|Sampdoria]],<ref name=":31" /><ref name=":41">{{Cite web |last=Boccacini |first=Gigi |date=10 July 1970 |title=Moschino al Verona, Frustalupi all'Inter |url=http://www.archiviolastampa.it/component/option,com_lastampa/task,search/mod,libera/action,viewer/Itemid,3/page,13/articleid,0132_01_1970_0138_0013_4815651/ |access-date=23 August 2023 |publisher=La Stampa |pages=13 |language=it-IT}}</ref> as part of a swap deal that saw [[Mario Frustalupi]] join Inter.<ref name=":41" /> In [[Genoa]], he moved back into his favoured position in midfield,<ref name=":31" /> and became one of the team's most notable players and leaders,<ref name=":31" /><ref name=":42">{{Cite web |last=Perucca |first=Bruno |date=27 September 1970 |title=Suarez si trova a suo agio come uomo-guida della Sampdoria |url=http://www.archiviolastampa.it/component/option,com_lastampa/task,search/mod,libera/action,viewer/Itemid,3/page,19/articleid,0133_01_1970_0205_0019_17976955/ |access-date=23 August 2023 |publisher=La Stampa |page=19 |language=it-IT}}</ref> together with [[Giovanni Lodetti]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":42" /> He scored 13 goals in 73 total appearances for the {{lang|it|Blucerchiati}}.<ref name=":43">{{Cite web |last=Pintimalli |first=Alessandro |date=9 July 2023 |title=Cordoglio blucerchiato per la scomparsa di Luis Suárez |url=https://www.sampdoria.it/news/club/2023/07/09/cordoglio-blucerchiato-per-la-scomparsa-di-luis-suarez/ |access-date=23 August 2023 |website=UC Sampdoria |language=it-IT}}</ref>

After completing three seasons at Sampdoria,<ref name=":9" /><ref name=":0" /> with the club managing to retain their top-flight status in each occasion,<ref name=":43" /> he announced his retirement from professional football in 1973, aged 38.<ref name=":8" /><ref name=":10" />

==International career==

Suárez won 32 caps for the [[Spain national football team|Spain senior national team]],<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":1" /> having made his debut on 30 January 1957 in a 5–1 victory over [[Netherlands national football team|the Netherlands]],<ref name=":3" /> and represented Spain at both the [[1962 FIFA World Cup squads#Spain|1962]] and [[1966 FIFA World Cup squads#Spain|1966]] [[FIFA World Cup]]s. He was part of the Spanish side that won the [[1964 European Nations' Cup|1964 European Championship]].<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":1" /> He played his final game for Spain in 1972, at almost 37 years of age, in a draw against [[Greece national football team|Greece]].<ref name=":16" /><ref name=":3" />

== Coaching career ==
Suárez managed his former team Inter Milan on three occasions: during the [[1974–75 Serie A|1974–75 season]] as a head coach, and then on a [[Caretaker manager|caretaker]] basis during the [[1991–92 Serie A|1991–92]] and [[1995–96 Serie A|1995–96]] campaigns.<ref name=":0" />

In 1986, he led the [[Spain national under-21 football team|Spain under-21 national team]] to a [[UEFA European Under-21 Championship|European Under-21 Championship]] title;<ref name=":14" /><ref name=":10" /> in 1990, he was the manager of the [[Spain national football team|Spanish senior national team]] at the [[1990 FIFA World Cup|1990 World Cup]], where they got eliminated in the round of 16.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":0" />

== Personal life ==
Suárez had two older brothers, {{ill|José Suárez Miramontes|gl|José Suárez Miramontes|lt=José}} (b. 1924) and {{ill|Agustín Suárez Miramontes|gl|Agustín Suárez Miramontes|lt=Agustín}} (b. 1926), who also played football, having both started their respective careers at Deportivo La Coruña.<ref name=":9" />

He married his first wife, Nieves, in 1967;<ref>{{Cite web |date=16 June 1967 |title=Se casó Luis Suárez |url=http://biblioteca.galiciana.gal/ |access-date=23 August 2023 |website=Galiciana |publisher=La Noche |page=11 |language=gl}}</ref> the couple had two children, and they lived in [[Nervi]], a {{lang|it|[[quartiere]]}} of Genoa, during the footballer's spell at Sampdoria and for several years following his retirement.<ref name=":45">{{Cite web |date=19 May 1977 |title=Morto il figlio (7 anni) dell'ex calciatore Suarez |url=http://www.archiviolastampa.it/component/option,com_lastampa/task,search/mod,libera/action,viewer/Itemid,3/page,11/articleid,1093_01_1977_0108_0011_15594877/ |access-date=23 August 2023 |publisher=La Stampa |page=11 |language=it-IT}}</ref> His younger son, who had been born with [[Cleft lip and cleft palate#Genetics|congenital cleft palate]], died in 1977, aged seven.<ref name=":45" />

Following a [[divorce]], he married his second wife, Valentina (who died in 2020);<ref name=":46">{{Cite web |last=Aguado |first=Antía S. |date=11 July 2023 |title=Italia rinde su último adiós a Luis Suárez, mito del Inter |url=https://www.lavozdegalicia.es/noticia/torremarathon/2023/07/11/italia-rinde-ultimo-adios-luis-suarez/00031689083838320778403.htm |access-date=23 August 2023 |website=La Voz de Galicia |language=es-ES}}</ref> the couple moved to [[Milan]] in 1988, settling in the {{lang|it|quartiere}} of [[San Siro, Milan|San Siro]], close to the [[San Siro|eponymous stadium]] Suárez had played in while at Inter Milan.<ref name=":24" />

=== Later life and personal achievements ===
In June 1989, he received the [[Castelao Medal]] by the [[Xunta de Galicia]] for his notable contributions in the sporting field.<ref>{{Cite web |date=9 July 2023 |title=La carrera de Luis Suárez en imágenes: adiós al mito gallego del fútbol |url=https://www.lavozdegalicia.es/album/deportes/2023/07/09/adios-mito-futbol-muere-luis-suarez-88-anos/01101688891917157244916.htm |access-date=23 August 2023 |website=La Voz de Galicia |language=es-ES}}</ref><ref name=":51">{{Cite web |date=9 July 2023 |title=Muere Luis Suárez Miramontes, el primer Balón de Oro de España |url=https://cadenaser.com/nacional/2023/07/09/muere-luis-suarez-miramontes-el-primer-balon-de-oro-de-espana-cadena-ser/ |access-date=23 August 2023 |website=[[Cadena SER]] |language=es-ES}}</ref>

Since the early 2000s, he worked as a guest [[pundit]] for several sports programmes broadcast on Italian and Spanish [[Television broadcaster|television networks]].<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=9 July 2023 |title=È morto Luisito Suárez, ex giocatore dell'Inter e opinionista televisivo |url=https://www.ilpost.it/2023/07/09/luisito-suarez-morto/ |access-date=23 August 2023 |website=Il Post |language=it-IT}}</ref>

On 20 November 2001,<ref name=":27" /> Suárez was awarded the Gold Medal of the [[Royal Order of Sports Merit|Royal Order of Sporting Merit]] by the [[Ministry of Education (Spain)|Ministry of Education, Culture and Sport]] for his sporting merits.<ref name=":10" /><ref name=":27" />

In 2008, he received the [[Golden Foot]] as a [[Golden Foot#Award legends|football legend]], together with [[Aldair]], [[Igor Belanov]] and [[Zinedine Zidane]].<ref name=":28" />

In 2014, he started working for [[Cadena SER]]'s radio programme {{lang|es|Carrusel Deportivo}},<ref name=":51" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=9 July 2023 |title='Carrusel' se despide de 'Don Luis': "Ha sido un privilegio tremendo, un regalo y una enseñanza" |url=https://cadenaser.com/nacional/2023/07/09/programa-especial-de-carrusel-deportivo-en-recuerdo-de-luis-suarez-miramontes-cadena-ser/ |access-date=23 August 2023 |website=Cadena SER |language=es-ES}}</ref> where he primarily served as a [[Sports commentator|commentator]] and an [[Sports analyst|analyst]] for Barcelona's matches.<ref name=":9" /><ref name=":51" />

In July 2015, as part of the celebrations for the 30th anniversary of the [[FC Barcelona Museum]], Suárez donated the Ballon d'Or trophy he received in 1961 to their collection.<ref name=":19" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=29 April 2015 |title=Luis Suárez cede su Balón de Oro al Barça |url=https://cadenaser.com/ser/2015/04/29/album/1430334018_410158.html |access-date=23 August 2023 |website=Cadena SER |language=es-ES}}</ref> On 14 December 2016, Spanish sports newspaper {{lang|es|[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]}} awarded him the [[Marca Leyenda|''Marca'' Leyenda]] prize for his career and achievements.<ref name=":44" /><ref name=":47" />

== Death ==
Suárez died on 9 July 2023, at the age of 88.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":0" /><ref name=":8" /> The news was first confirmed by former Inter Milan president [[Massimo Moratti]], who revealed the former player and manager had been hospitalized at the [[Ospedale Niguarda Ca' Granda|Ospedale Niguarda]] in Milan several days before his death.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=9 July 2023 |title=Inter in lutto, è morto Luisito Suarez |url=https://www.lapresse.it/calcio/2023/07/09/inter-in-lutto-e-morto-luisito-suarez/ |access-date=10 July 2023 |website=LaPresse |language=it-IT}}</ref> He was the fourth 1964 European Nations' Cup champion to die in a few months, after [[Amancio (footballer)|Amancio]] died in February 2023, [[Josep Maria Fusté|Fusté]] in April 2023 and [[Ferran Olivella|Olivella]] in May 2023.

A public funeral was held on 11 July, at the [[Saint Joseph Calasanz]] Church in Milan: the service was attended by several fans,<ref name=":46" /><ref name=":48">{{Cite web |date=11 July 2023 |title=A Milano l'ultimo saluto a Luisito Suarez |url=https://sport.sky.it/calcio/serie-a/2023/07/11/inter-suarez-funerali |access-date=23 August 2023 |website=Sky Sport |language=it-IT}}</ref> as well as representatives from Barcelona (Rafa Yuste and [[Juan Manuel Asensi]]),<ref name=":46" /> Inter Milan ([[Gianfranco Bedin]], Massimo Moratti and [[Giuseppe Marotta]])<ref name=":48" /> and Real Madrid ([[Emilio Butragueño]]).<ref name=":46" /><ref name=":48" /> Deportivo La Coruña, Real and the [[Royal Spanish Football Federation|Spanish Football Federation]] all reportedly sent flower garlands to pay homage to Suárez.<ref name=":46" /><ref name=":48" />
